rows.title: Bokashi Ingredients

intro_text.eng: Remember to turn **Bokashi** twice in a day for the first three days to regulate the temperature. From the 4th day turn it ones daily for the next 11 days. It will be ready after 14 days.

ing_transcript.eng:
3 wheelbarrows of topsoil... introduces beneficial microorganisms that help start decomposition.
3 wheelbarrows of dry materials... provide carbon and improve aeration for microbial activity.
3 wheelbarrows of manure... supply nitrogen to support rapid microbial growth.
9 to 12 spades of bran... act as food to multiply beneficial microorganisms.
9 to 12 spades of biochar... help improve water retention and soil structure. It also helps hold nutrients needed by crops... protecting the compost from leaching and evaporation.
Yeast or sourdough starter... helps speed up the fermentation process.
Water... enough to maintain the moisture needed for active microbial processes.
2 litres of molasses... or 2 kilograms of overripe fruits... or 20 litres of coffee water... provide quick energy to boost microbial activity.
Rock dust... ash... or phosphite... add important minerals like potassium and silicon to enrich the soil.

rows.title: Ash Brew Ingredients

ing_transcript.eng:
10kg of hardwood ash, well sifted to remove large charcoal chunks, preventing the clogging of the sprayer nozzle. Ash provides high levels of potassium and silica, which help strengthen plant cell walls against sucking pests.

1kg of bar soap. It is important to avoid soaps with chemicals and detergents. The soap acts as a surfactant, helping the solution stick to insects and cling to waxy leaf surfaces.

40ltr of water are used to dilute the solution, ensuring it is gentle enough not to scorch young, tender leaves while still remaining toxic to pests.

The boiling process helps accelerate the extraction of active minerals and ensures the soap dissolves into a uniform solution.

storage_transcript.eng:
* Take out liquid and store in a drum.
* Use remaining solids for washing dishes.

usage_transcript.eng:
* Apply when the weather is cool (i.e., evening or morning)
* Add 2 litres of cooking oil immediately after brewing
* Oil makes it more efficient in controlling insects with a waxy body or scales
* This practice increases photosynthesis rates.

rows.title: Tephrosia Solution Ingredients

step_1_text.eng:
* 5 kg of fresh Tephrosia leaves that are about to flower.
 * 20 liters of water.

transcript.eng:
* **Tephrosia Leaves:** Contain the highest concentration of rotenone, the natural chemical that paralyzes pests.
 * **Pounding/Crushing:** Breaks down plant fibers to release the active insecticidal compounds into the water.
 * **Shade Drying:** If storing leaves, dry them out of direct sunlight to prevent the UV rays from breaking down the active chemicals.
 * **Late Afternoon Spraying:** Prevents the solution from evaporating too quickly and protects beneficial pollinators like bees.
 * **Straining:** Using a fine cloth ensures a smooth liquid that won't block manual or knapsack sprayers.

rows.title: Garlic Water Ingredients

step_1_text.eng:
* 10 cloves of garlic
 * 2 ginger roots or 100g of ginger
 * 2 tablespoons of bar soap/Neem oil
 * 10 red peppers (medium size)
 * 1 litre of clean water
 * Pestle and a mortar/gretor

transcript.eng:
* **Crushed Cloves:** Releases Allicin, the strong-smelling compound that confuses and repels searching pests.
 * **Soaking Time:** Allows for maximum infusion of oils into the water for a more potent repellent.
 * **Vegetable Oil (Optional):** Helps the garlic scent linger longer on the plants after application.
 * **Small Batch Usage:** Best used within 24 hours, as the active repellent compounds degrade quickly once exposed to air.
 * **Targeted Application:** Focus on the undersides of leaves where aphids and mites typically congregate.

rows.title:
Fermented feeds 
Ingredients

ing_transcript.eng:
Carbohydrates sources 70%
Examples; cereals -maize, millet, sorghum, wheat, oats, rice etc. Grain by products ie maize bran , maize germ, wheat bran, wheat Pollard, rice bran etc.
Root crops- cassava, sweet potatoes, arrow roots, yams 
Fruits : cooking banana variety

Proteins sources 25%
Azolla, legumes ie soya , lablab, cowpea, pegion pea, common beans etc, fodder shrubs leaves ie calliandra, sesbania, leucaena, Gliricidia, mulberry, moringa etc
Fishmeal, cotton cake, sunflower cake, pumpkin seeds,grain amaranth, blood meal etc.,

Vitamin and mineral sources 5%
Leafy vegetables, well ripened fruits ie banana, jackfruit, white sapote, custard apple,,mango, pineapple etc. Pumpkin ,,,
Stockfed lime, Dicalcium phosphate, egg shells, sea salt/table salt, burnt animal bones etc. 

Others
Molasses,microbes, water, weeds(blackjack, gallant soldiers, wandering Jews), banana leaves, banana stems (young or white inner part), grasses ( Nappier), comfrey leaves 

" * **Molasses:** is a source of energy for microbes. Drives the fermentation process and improves the taste of the feed when fed to the birds.
 * Microbes turn fresh feed into a safe, preserved, and more nutritious feed by controlling fermentation.
 * Microbes can be added to drinking water or sprayed in the poultry house to reduce the ammonia smell.
 * To get the birds used to the taste and smell of the fermented feeds, at first mix with other feeds for a period of 1 week or 2 then they will love the feeds and there will be no wastage.
 * Fermented feeds can be used as a daily diet or on occasion.

storage_transcript.eng: Store the container in a cool and dry place free from rats and direct sunlight or disturbances.

Homemade chickmash
Ingredients

intro_text.eng: When mixing the ingredients, start with the heaviest and finish with the lightest.

step_1_text.eng:
* Maize (njenga) - 12kg 
 * Maize bran (Ngozi ya mahindi) - 3kg
 * Maize germ (moyo) - 3kg 
 * Wheat/rice bran - 3kg 
 * Soya (njenga) - 4kg 
 * Sunflower white or black (oil extracted) - 2.17 kg 
 * Fishmeal - 1.33 kg 
 * DCP - 0.3 kg 
 * Lime (calcium) - 0.4 kg 
 * Salt - 0.1 kg 
 * Chick premix - 0.3kg 
 * Lysine - 0.1 kg 
 * Methionine -  0.1kg 
 * Toxin binder - 0.2kg

transcript.eng:

 * **Soya (njenga), Sunflower, Fishmeal:** Provide proteins for body building
 * **DCP & Lime:**  phosphorus and calcium for strong bones and eggshells
 * **Salt:** Provides sodium and chloride for body balance
 * **Chick premix:** Source of vitamins and trace minerals
 * **Toxin binders:** Breaks harmful toxins into harmless parts.
 * **Lysine and methionine:** Essential amino acids needed for growth.
 * Supplements of DCP are crushed eggshells or bones .

storage_transcript.eng: Store in a cool and dry place

step_1_text.eng:
* Ginger - Thumb size 
 * Tumeric - thumbnail  
 * Hot pepper 4- 5 
 * Garlic - 2 cloves 
 * Tithonia leaves - handful  
 * Aloe Vera  - 2-4

transcript.eng:
* **Ginger:** Acts as a natural stimulant and antimicrobial agent that supports digestion and disease resistance.
 * **Turmeric:** Suppresses harmful microbes during fermentation and improves the medicinal value of the concoction.
 * **Hot peppers (chillies):** Contain capsaicin, which acts as a natural pest repellent and antimicrobial agent. They also help deter insects and harmful organisms.
 * **Garlic:** Enhances disease control and improves the overall effectiveness of the mixture.
 * **Tithonia leaves:** Improve the nutritional value of the mixture and support microbial fermentation.
 * **Aloe vera:** Contains enzymes and bioactive compounds that support fermentation and improve the stability of the mixture.
 * **Water:** Allows proper fermentation or dilution for application.

rows.title: Silage Making Ingredients

step_1_text.eng:
* Fodder materials to be preserved, eg, Napier
* Maize bran - CHO reduces the moisture content
* Molasses
* Chaff cutter/panga
* Airtight container

transcript.eng:
* **Fodder materials:** Provides bulk, nutrients, and fiber needed for good-quality livestock feed after fermentation.
 * **Maize bran:** Absorb excess moisture from the fodder and provides carbohydrates that support fermentation.
 * **Molasses:** Acts as a fermentation booster while improving taste and energy value.
 * Chopping fodder into small pieces increases compaction, removes air spaces, and speeds up fermentation.
 * **Airtight container (e.g., silo, polythene bag, drum):** This is used to exclude air. 
 * Silage fermentation must occur in anaerobic (oxygen-free) conditions; otherwise, the fodder will rot instead of fermenting. 
* Silage making relies on chopping fodder, balancing moisture, adding energy sources, and sealing everything airtight to allow beneficial fermentation and prevent spoilage.

storage_transcript.eng:
* Keep the silage in airtight conditions.
You can use:
   * Paper bags
   * Skyplast bags
   * Hermetic bags
 * Airtight storage ensures proper preservation and long shelf life.

rows.title: Mulching Ingredients

intro_text.eng: Mulching helps to conserve soil moisture, suppress weed growth, and improve soil health as organic materials decompose over time.

step_1_text.eng:
* Dry leaves
 * Grass clippings
 * Straw/hay
 * Sawdust/Wood chips
 * Farmyard manure/compost
 * Water

transcript.eng:
* **Dry leaves, grass clippings, straw, hay:** Provide a protective cover that suppresses weeds by blocking sunlight and conserves moisture by reducing evaporation.
 * **Wood chips / sawdust:** Improve soil structure over time and provide long-term coverage to regulate soil temperature.
 * **Farmyard manure / compost:** Enhances soil fertility and adds organic matter as it decomposes.
 * **Water:** Helps settle the mulch and ensures the underlying soil remains hydrated to support beneficial soil organisms.
 * **Temperature Regulation:** Insulates the soil, keeping it cooler in the summer and warmer in the winter to protect plant roots.
 * **Soil Erosion Control:** Acts as a physical barrier to shield the soil from the direct impact of raindrops and wind.

rows.title: Zai Pit Ingredients

intro_text.eng: Zai pits help harvest runoff water and concentrate manure or compost, allowing crops to thrive in dry or degraded soils.

step_1_text.eng:
* 2-3 handfuls (200g - 600g) of organic fertilisers or compost 
 * Manure
 * Dry plant biomass
 * Topsoil

step_2_text.eng:
* 1 bucket of Compost or well-rotted Manure 
 * 1 bucket of Dry plant biomass or Mulch 
 * 1 bucket of Topsoil (for covering)

transcript.eng:
* **Organic Material (Manure/Compost/Dry Biomass):** Attracts termites and microorganisms that improve soil structure and nutrient availability.
 * **Water Harvesting:** The pits act as micro-catchments that trap rainfall and runoff, reducing water stress during droughts.
 * **Nutrient Concentration:** Placing amendments directly in the pit prevents them from being washed away and focuses fertility near the crop roots.
 * **Topsoil Ridges:** Excavated soil formed into ridges helps capture additional runoff and directs it into the pits.
 * **Termite Activity:** Termites digging channels in the soil increase water infiltration and speed up the decomposition of organic matter.
 * **Soil Rehabilitation:** Breaks up hardpan layers, making degraded or encrusted land productive again.

rows.title: Sunken Bed Ingredients

intro_text.eng: A sunken bed helps to collect and conserve water, making it ideal for growing vegetables in dry or arid areas.

step_1_text.eng:
* Topsoil 
 * Well-rotted manure or compost 
 * Dry organic matter (leaves, grass) 
 * Water

transcript.eng:
* **Topsoil:** Provides the base for the bed and introduces native microorganisms.
 * **Well-rotted manure or compost:** Boosts soil fertility, improves structure, and adds organic matter to support plant health.
 * **Dry organic matter (leaves or grass):** Acts as a carbon source and mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
 * **Water:** Concentrates in the recessed area to ensure deep infiltration and keep roots cool.
 * **Protective Profile:** The sunken design shields plants from drying winds and helps regulate soil temperature.
